KubernetesJobProfile.description:
The bundle of fields the workflow's kubernetes_job code path needs to build a pytest Job pod.

Attached to providers that resolve to ``kubernetes_job`` mode so the selector can fail at selection time
when a cluster_internal provider lacks its profile, instead of failing late inside the Job step with an empty
image/service setup.

service.description: Service name used both for the Docker image build and as the K8s service identity.
service.title: Service

service_account.description: ServiceAccount used by the Job for IAM/IRSA.
service_account.title: Service Account

config_map.description: Name of the ConfigMap to mount as env. Resolved by the consumer when omitted.
config_map.title: Config Map

timeout_seconds.description: Active deadline for the Job pod.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

KubernetesJobProfile.title: KubernetesJobProfile

Placement.description:
Reduction of a test's required-providers list to a CI matrix entry.

The selector calls :func:`placement_for` per test (or per group of tests
sharing identical placements) and emits one matrix entry per unique
placement. The workflow then computes its ``env:`` block from
:attr:`secrets`, its ``services:`` block from :attr:`services`, and picks
the runner vs k8s-job code path from :attr:`mode`.

secrets.description: Sorted, deduplicated list of secret env-var names the *runner* must export. Cluster-internal providers contribute via :attr:`cluster_secrets` instead — those are mounted by the cluster, not by GitHub Actions.
secrets.title: Secrets

cluster_secrets.description: Sorted, deduplicated list of env-var names the in-cluster Job needs from its service ConfigMap. Documentation only — the workflow doesn't pass them, the cluster mounts them. Runner providers' ``runner_secrets`` are promoted here when the placement is k8s mode.
cluster_secrets.title: Cluster Secrets

runtime_env.description: Aggregated static env vars the workflow exports after services are up. Union of every chosen provider's ``runtime_env``; conflicting values for the same key raise.
runtime_env.title: Runtime Env

env_scope.description: Strictest env binding across required providers.
env_scope.title: Env Scope

Placement.title: Placement

Provider.description:
One concrete way to satisfy a :class:`Resource`.

Providers are ordered within a Resource by *preference* (cheapest first).
The framework resolves a test's ``requires(...)`` to the first provider
that is *available* in the current environment (see
:func:`is_provider_available`). Tests can pin a specific provider with
``provider="..."`` when they genuinely need that flavour (e.g. a Lua-script
test that fakeredis can't execute).

Combinations of fields encode the placement decision:

* ``cluster_internal=True`` — placement is forced to ``kubernetes_job``;
  ``runner_secrets`` must be empty (the runner never holds them) and
  ``cluster_secrets`` documents what the in-cluster Job needs from its
  service ConfigMap.
* Every provider is assumed runnable in the target Kubernetes environment.
  If the runner cannot satisfy ``runner_secrets`` but the selector chooses
  k8s execution, those names are treated as target-env ConfigMap/Secret
  requirements instead of GitHub Actions requirements.
* ``service_container is not None`` — placement adds a ``services:`` entry on the runner.
* ``runner_secrets`` non-empty — those secrets must be exported on the runner;
  provider counts as available only when every name is present (and non-empty)
  in the workflow's ``available_secrets`` list (unless we're resolving in
  cluster mode, where target-env config is authoritative).
* ``runtime_env`` — env vars consumers expect when this provider is the
  chosen one. The workflow's "Start placement services" step exports them
  after the service container is healthy, so tests don't need to special-
  case "is fakeredis or real Redis" — both expose ``GV_REDIS_HOST`` etc.
* ``env_scope != "any"`` — provider only resolves in that target environment.

name.description: Human-readable provider id, unique within its Resource. Tests pin via ``provider=<name>``.
name.title: Name

runner_secrets.description: Env-var names that must be present (non-empty) on the runner for this provider to be available. Only meaningful for runner-mode providers — by definition the runner can't carry secrets that only exist inside the target Kubernetes cluster.
runner_secrets.title: Runner Secrets

cluster_secrets.description: Env-var names this provider's tests will read from the target environment's service ConfigMap when running as a Kubernetes Job. Documentation only — the cluster mounts these, the runner never sees them. Only meaningful for cluster_internal=True providers.
cluster_secrets.title: Cluster Secrets

runtime_env.description: Static env vars the workflow exports after this provider's services are up. Consumed by tests via the ordinary env mechanism — e.g. fakeredis declares ``{}`` so consumers fall through to their default Redis host, while ``redis-ephemeral`` declares ``{'GV_REDIS_HOST': 'localhost', 'GV_REDIS_PORT': '6379'}`` so the same test code reads the right host without a plugin mutating env at collection time.
runtime_env.title: Runtime Env

service_container.description: Runner-side ephemeral container, if this provider needs one. Mutually compatible with ``runner_secrets`` (a containerized Postgres still might need a password env var).

cluster_internal.description: True if this provider needs Kubernetes execution — in-cluster DNS, deployed services, or namespace ConfigMaps. Forces ``kubernetes_job`` mode.
cluster_internal.title: Cluster Internal

kubernetes_job_profile.description: Required when ``cluster_internal=True`` — declares the image/service/config-map/timeout the workflow needs to build a Job pod. Without this, the selector fails fast instead of letting the Job step run with an empty image setup.

env_scope.description: Target environment binding. ``any`` resolves under any active env; ``dev`` / ``stg`` / ``prd`` only resolve when the runner targets that env.
env_scope.title: Env Scope

Provider.title: Provider

ServiceContainer.description:
Definition of a runner-side ephemeral container — maps 1:1 to one entry of GitHub Actions' ``services:`` block.

Provided by ephemeral providers (``image=redis:7-alpine``, etc.) so the
framework can spin up real-but-disposable infrastructure on the runner
without paying the k8s round-trip.

service_name.description: Key under ``services:`` in the resulting workflow YAML. Used as the deduplication key when multiple providers contribute containers — two containers with the same service_name is a configuration error.
service_name.title: Service Name

env.description: Environment variables passed into the container.
env.title: Env

credentials.description: Registry credentials for pulling private images.
credentials.title: Credentials

ServiceContainer.title: ServiceContainer
